analysis.investment_thesis: Ion Exchange is a legitimate water-treatment story riding India's secular pollution-control and ZLD regulatory tailwind, with an impressive 32% net profit CAGR over nine years. However, the PEG ratio is stretched (~1.75x using trailing P/E of 30.3 ÷ ~17% 5-year earnings CAGR), net profit growth has stalled (INR 195 Cr in FY24 vs. INR 208 Cr in FY25, only +6.7%), and free cash flow collapsed to -INR 287 Cr in FY25 — this is not GARP territory yet.
key_strengths: Secular mega-trend: India's tightening ZLD/effluent norms and Jal Jeevan Mission directly drive demand for all three segments (Engineering, Chemicals, Consumer)
Long compounding track record: Revenue 13.6% CAGR and EBITDA 19.1% CAGR over 9 years with zero down-revenue years, proving cycle resilience
Capital efficiency improving: ROCE of 22.3% and D/E of only 0.32 despite a major capex cycle underway (CWIP surged to INR 203 Cr)
key_risks: PEG ~1.75 is well above Lynch's 1.0 comfort zone, making the stock expensive for its current growth rate — especially with near-term earnings momentum fading
Operating margins are razor-thin at 5.54%, leaving almost no buffer if raw-material costs or competitive pricing pressure intensifies in the project-engineering segment
FCF turned deeply negative (-INR 287 Cr in FY25) while borrowings tripled from INR 62 Cr (FY21) to INR 421 Cr (FY25) — the capex bet must pay off or the balance sheet deteriorates fast
red_flags: Net profit growth deceleration: INR 195 Cr → INR 208 Cr (+6.7%) in FY25 after stellar prior-year growth — the story is visibly weakening near-term
Promoter stake of only 25.58% is low for a mid-cap; limited skin-in-the-game relative to the capex risk being taken
Operating CF of only INR 32 Cr vs. net profit of INR 208 Cr in FY25 signals aggressive working-capital consumption — earnings quality is deteriorating
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Ion Exchange is exactly the kind of niche industrial compounder I love to find early — a company in an essential, regulation-driven industry where the customer has no choice but to invest. India's factories must comply with ZLD norms; municipalities need water treatment; the captive demand is real. The 9-year record of expanding EBITDA from INR 71 Cr to INR 342 Cr at 19% CAGR, with consistent revenue growth through COVID, confirms this is not a cyclical flash-in-the-pan. At INR 4,932 Cr market cap, it still has room to be a multi-bagger if management executes the current capex cycle well.

That said, the numbers right now don't justify a buy at 30x trailing earnings. Lynch's rule of thumb is P/E shouldn't be more than 2x the growth rate — here P/E 30 vs. ~15-17% sustainable growth gives a PEG of ~1.75, firmly in "overpriced for the story" territory. More worrying: FCF went from +INR 167 Cr (FY21) to -INR 287 Cr (FY25) as capex exploded to INR 320 Cr, while operating CF shrank to just INR 32 Cr. Borrowings tripled in two years. The investment thesis only works if the CWIP of INR 203 Cr converts into revenue and margin expansion over FY26-27, unlocking the forward P/E of 22.3x. Watch operating margins and FCF normalization before adding aggressively — this is a "put on the watchlist, revisit after one earnings cycle" situation.
